questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text:
Consider the following statements about the Standing Deposit Facility:
I. Apart from liquidity management, RBI describes the SDF as a financial stability tool.
II. Deposits under the SDF are eligible assets for maintaining SLR but are not reckoned for CRR.
III. RBI can use the SDF only for overnight deposits and never for longer tenors.
Which of the above is/are correct?

solution.explanation: RBI states that the SDF is also a financial stability tool (I correct). SDF deposits are not reckoned for CRR under Section 42 of the RBI Act but are eligible for SLR under Section 24 of the BR Act (II correct). RBI retains the flexibility to absorb liquidity for longer tenors under the SDF with appropriate pricing (III wrong).

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: In September 1962, RBI fixed the Cash Reserve Ratio uniformly at what level, and with what flexibility to vary it?

options.text: 5% of demand liabilities and 2% of time liabilities, fixed

3% of demand and time liabilities, variable between 3% and 15%

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness

Section 35A of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949
Section 18(1) of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: A bank has demand liabilities of ₹400 crore and time liabilities of ₹600 crore. What cash reserve would it have needed under the requirement applied to scheduled banks from 5 July 1935, and how does that compare with a 3% CRR on its total liabilities?

options.text: ₹32 crore, which is ₹2 crore more than under a 3% CRR
₹30 crore, the same as under a 3% CRR
₹50 crore, which is ₹20 crore more than under a 3% CRR
₹20 crore, which is ₹10 crore less than under a 3% CRR

solution.explanation: From 5 July 1935 scheduled banks had to hold cash with RBI equal to 5% of demand liabilities and 2% of time liabilities: 5% × 400 + 2% × 600 = 20 + 12 = ₹32 crore. A 3% CRR on ₹1,000 crore = ₹30 crore. Difference = ₹2 crore more under the 1935 rule.
solution.why_others_wrong: ₹50 crore applies 5% to everything; ₹20 crore counts only demand liabilities; ₹30 crore is the 3% figure.
solution.final_answer: Option A: ₹32 crore, which is ₹2 crore more than under a 3% CRR

fact_checks.claim: 5 Jul 1935: Scheduled banks required to maintain the Cash Reserve Ratio, i.e., hold cash balances with the RBI equivalent to 5% of their Demand Liabilities and 2% of their Time Liabilities

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: A bank's required average CRR balance for a fortnight is ₹900 crore. Its average balance in its current account with RBI was ₹850 crore, and it also kept an average of ₹100 crore overnight under the Standing Deposit Facility. What is its CRR position?

options.text: Short by ₹50 crore, because SDF deposits are not reckoned for CRR
Short by ₹150 crore, because SDF deposits are deducted from the CRR balance
Surplus of ₹50 crore, because SDF deposits count towards CRR

solution.explanation: Deposits under the SDF are not reckoned as balances eligible for CRR maintenance under Section 42 of the RBI Act (they are eligible for SLR). So only ₹850 crore counts: 900 − 850 = ₹50 crore shortfall.
solution.why_others_wrong: Counting the SDF gives a false surplus; it is neither compliant nor penalised by deducting the SDF amount.
solution.final_answer: Option A: Short by ₹50 crore, because SDF deposits are not reckoned for CRR

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness

Accept overnight deposits from banks without collateral
Pay interest on banks' CRR balances

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: How does RBI describe the role of the Marginal Standing Facility (MSF) in the liquidity framework?

options.text: The operating target of monetary policy
A long-term refinance window for priority sectors
The floor of the LAF corridor for absorbing surplus liquidity
A penal-rate overnight window that acts as a safety valve against unanticipated liquidity shocks

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: The MSF was introduced with effect from 9 May 2011. How did its design at launch differ from the present one?

It was raised at every meeting, ending 0.6 percentage point above the April projection
It was raised in June and October only, ending 0.4 percentage point above April
It was cut in June and raised in August and October

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: Under RBI's prudential norms, a 'loss asset' is one where:

options.text: Interest is overdue for more than 90 days
Loss has been identified by the bank, its auditors or RBI inspection, but the amount has not been written off wholly
The asset has been substandard for 12 months
The account has been written off fully

solution.explanation: RBI defines a loss asset as an asset where loss has been identified by the bank or internal or external auditors or RBI inspection, but the amount has not been written off wholly. steps: Loss identified + not fully written off → loss asset

When the account is overdue for more than three days
When the card is not used for 90 days

As SMA-2, until P transfers the funds
As NPA, because the account is treated as not serviced in their books
As standard, because the borrower is paying the consortium

solution.explanation: Asset classification under consortium lending depends on each member's own record of recovery. Where remittances are pooled with one member that does not part with the others' shares, the account is treated as not serviced in the books of the other members and therefore as NPA. Members should get their share transferred from the lead bank or obtain its express consent.
steps: Classification follows each member's own recovery
No share received → not serviced → NPA for Q and R
solution.why_others_wrong: Payment to the lead bank alone does not service Q's and R's loans; P is being paid; SMA-2 is not the rule here.
solution.final_answer: Option C: As NPA, because the account is treated as not serviced in their books

Only at the end of each financial year

questions.question_text:
Consider the following statements about the retail e₹ as described in RBI's FAQs:
I. A P2P or P2M payment made at a CBDC QR code moves between two e₹ wallets and settles instantly without passing through the users' bank accounts.
II. When a UPI QR is scanned from an e₹ app, settlement follows UPI settlement timelines.
III. e₹ payments must be in whole rupees.
Which of the above is/are correct?

solution.explanation: RBI states that P2P and P2M payments at a CBDC QR happen between two e₹ wallets and settle instantaneously without passing through bank accounts (I correct); payments made by scanning a UPI QR from an e₹ app settle on UPI timelines (II correct); e₹ supports payments up to two decimal places (III wrong).
solution.why_others_wrong: III is false, so options including it are wrong; 'I only' omits II.
solution.final_answer: Option C: I and II only

fact_checks.claim: Payments at any CBDC QR happen between two e₹ wallets and are settled instantaneously without passing through user's bank accounts; scanning a UPI QR from an e₹ app settles on UPI settlement timelines; e₹ supports payments up to two decimal places

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text:
Consider the following statements under the RBI (Digital Lending) Directions, 2025:
I. Lending through digital lending apps must be reported to credit information companies irrespective of its nature or tenor.
II. Short-term deferred payment ('buy now, pay later') products offered over merchant platforms need not be reported to CICs.
III. If a borrower's complaint gets no reply from the lender within 30 days, the borrower can complain under the RB-IOS.
Which of the above is/are correct?

solution.concept: Credit reporting and grievances in digital lending
solution.explanation: Lending through DLAs must be reported to CICs irrespective of nature or tenor (I correct). Structured digital lending products over merchant platforms involving short-term credits or deferred payments must also be reported to CICs (II wrong). If the RE rejects a complaint or does not reply within 30 days, the borrower can complain under RB-IOS (III correct).
solution.why_others_wrong: II contradicts the Directions; 'I only' omits III.
solution.final_answer: Option B: I and III only

fact_checks.claim: RE shall ensure that any lending done through DLAs is reported to CICs irrespective of its nature/tenor; structured digital lending products over a merchant platform involving short term credits or deferred payments need to be reported to CICs; if no reply within 30 days, the borrower can lodge a complaint under RB-IOS

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: Under RBI's Digital Banking Channels Authorisation Directions, 2025, which statement about a 'view only' digital banking facility is correct?

options.text: It may offer fund transfers but not loans
Only banks with a net worth above ₹1,000 crore may offer it
A bank with CBS and IPv6-enabled public-facing IT may launch it without prior approval, intimating RBI within 30 days with a GAICA report
It needs RBI's prior approval through PRAVAAH, like a transactional facility

solution.explanation: View-only facilities allow only services that do not change the customer's assets or liabilities (balance, statements). Banks with CBS and IPv6-enabled public-facing IT are eligible, and must intimate RBI through PRAVAAH, with a Gap Assessment and Internal Controls Adequacy (GAICA) report, within 30 days of deciding to launch. Prior approval is needed only for transactional facilities.
steps: Intimation within 30 days with GAICA report
solution.why_others_wrong: Prior approval applies to transactional facilities; fund transfers are excluded from view-only; no ₹1,000 crore net worth test exists.
solution.final_answer: Option C: A bank with CBS and IPv6-enabled public-facing IT may launch it without prior approval, intimating RBI within 30 days with a GAICA report

fact_checks.claim: All banks which have implemented CBS and have enabled their public facing IT infrastructure to handle IPv6 traffic are eligible to provide view only banking facility; shall intimate the Department of Regulation through PRAVAAH, along with a copy of the GAICA report, within thirty days; loans and funds transfers cannot be provided with view only facility

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: According to RBI's Payment System Report of May 2026, what share of the total volume of payment transactions in the second half of calendar year 2025 was accounted for by UPI?

solution.explanation: In H2 of CY 2025, UPI accounted for 85.5% of transaction volume, followed by NEFT and PPIs (3.6% each), with RTGS at 0.1%. By value, RTGS dominated with 68.6%, NEFT 14.9% and UPI 9.5%.
solution.why_others_wrong: 68.6% is RTGS's value share; 9.5% is UPI's value share; 3.6% is NEFT's or PPIs' volume share.

fact_checks.claim: In H2 of CY 2025, UPI commanded the largest share of transaction volume at 85.5 per cent... RTGS dominated value with 68.6 per cent... UPI at 9.5 per cent

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: Which UPI-based innovation, listed by RBI alongside UPI 123Pay and UPI Circle, enables cardless cash withdrawals?

solution.explanation: RBI's Payment System Report lists innovations that expanded UPI: UPI 123Pay for feature phones, Hello UPI for voice payments, UPI-ATM for cardless cash withdrawals, Credit Card on UPI and UPI Circle.
solution.why_others_wrong: Hello UPI is voice-based payments; UPI Lite is for small-value on-device payments; BHIM Aadhaar Pay is a merchant payment mode.

fact_checks.claim: Innovations such as UPI 123Pay (for feature phones), Hello UPI (voice-enabled payments), UPI-ATM (cardless cash withdrawals), Credit Card on UPI, and UPI Circle

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: According to RBI's Payment System Report of May 2026, the number of UPI transactions rose from 3,873 crore in CY 2021 to how many in CY 2025?

solution.explanation: UPI volumes grew from 3,873 crore transactions in CY 2021 to 22,828 crore in CY 2025, and value from ₹72 lakh crore to ₹300 lakh crore — a CAGR of 55.8% in volume and 43% in value.
solution.why_others_wrong: The other figures do not match RBI's data.

fact_checks.claim: The volume of UPI transactions has increased from 3,873 crore transactions in CY 2021 to 22,828 crore transactions in CY 2025; value grew from ₹72 lakh crore to ₹300 lakh crore

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: Which multilateral initiative for international remittances does RBI mention alongside bilateral links between UPI and other countries' fast payment systems?

solution.explanation: RBI's report says UPI and Singapore's PayNow have been linked since February 2023, similar bilateral integrations are under way, and the multilateral Project Nexus is ongoing for international remittances.
solution.why_others_wrong: The other names are not the multilateral fast-payment initiative named by RBI.

fact_checks.claim: Similar integrations with other national fast payment systems are currently underway, alongside the ongoing multilateral Project Nexus for international remittances

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: What compound annual growth rates did UPI record from CY 2021 to CY 2025, according to RBI?

solution.explanation: RBI's report gives UPI's CAGR over CY 2021–2025 as 55.8% in volume and 43% in value. The 43%/17% pair is the CAGR for all digital payments over the last five years, and 4.5%/18.1% is IMPS.
solution.why_others_wrong: The second option swaps the two; the other pairs belong to overall digital payments or IMPS.
solution.final_answer: Option C: 55.8% in volume and 43% in value

fact_checks.claim: The CAGR of the UPI transaction during this period is 55.8 per cent in terms of volume and 43 per cent in terms of value

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: In UPI and IMPS, funds reach the beneficiary immediately. How is the inter-bank settlement done?

options.text: Gross and in real time in RBI's books for each transaction
Only when the beneficiary withdraws cash
Later, on a deferred net basis according to a pre-defined settlement cycle

solution.explanation: RBI explains that in systems like UPI and IMPS the beneficiary is credited immediately, while the inter-bank settlement happens later according to a pre-defined settlement cycle — deferred net settlement. In RTGS, by contrast, each transaction settles gross and in real time.
solution.why_others_wrong: Gross real-time settlement describes RTGS; NACH and cash withdrawal are irrelevant.
solution.final_answer: Option D: Later, on a deferred net basis according to a pre-defined settlement cycle

fact_checks.claim: In a few systems like UPI and IMPS, while funds are credited to the beneficiary customer immediately, the inter-bank settlement is done later according to a pre-defined settlement cycle... Deferred Settlement

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: UPI processed 22,828 crore transactions worth ₹300 lakh crore in CY 2025. What is the approximate average ticket size, and how does it compare with CY 2021, when it was ₹1,848?

solution.explanation: ₹300 lakh crore = 300 × 10⁵ crore = 3,00,00,000 crore rupees. Dividing by 22,828 crore transactions gives ≈ ₹1,314 per transaction (RBI reports ₹1,313). This is below ₹1,848 in CY 2021, showing UPI's growing use for small payments.
solution.why_others_wrong: ₹13,140 and ₹131 misplace the decimal; ₹1,314 is lower, not higher, than ₹1,848.
solution.final_answer: Option C: About ₹1,314, lower than in 2021

fact_checks.claim: Total value ₹300 lakh crore in CY 2025; 22,828 crore transactions; average ticket size declined from ₹1,848 in CY 2021 to ₹1313 in CY 2025

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: By value, UPI accounted for only 9.5% of payment transactions in H2 of CY 2025. Which systems ranked above it by value?

options.text: No system; UPI ranked first by value too

solution.explanation: RBI's report shows that by value RTGS dominated with 68.6%, followed by NEFT at 14.9% and UPI at 9.5%, with PPIs at 0.1%. UPI leads by volume (85.5%) because it handles mass, small-value retail payments.
solution.why_others_wrong: IMPS, NACH, PPIs and cards were not ranked above UPI by value; UPI leads only by volume.

fact_checks.claim: In terms of transaction value, RTGS dominated with 68.6 per cent of the total transaction value, followed by NEFT at 14.9 per cent and UPI at 9.5 per cent, with PPIs contributing only 0.1 per cent

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: Who owns and operates the National Electronic Funds Transfer (NEFT) system?

solution.explanation: RBI's FAQs describe NEFT as a nation-wide centralised payment system owned and operated by the Reserve Bank of India. NPCI operates retail systems such as IMPS and UPI.
steps: NEFT → owned and operated by RBI
solution.why_others_wrong: NPCI runs IMPS/UPI/NACH; IBA and IDRBT do not operate NEFT.
solution.final_answer: Option A: Reserve Bank of India

fact_checks.claim: National Electronic Funds Transfer (NEFT) is a nation-wide centralised payment system owned and operated by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI)

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: In the NEFT transaction flow, after the originating bank prepares the payment message, where does it send it first?

options.text: To the RTGS Member Interface for gross settlement
To its pooling centre (NEFT Service Centre), which forwards it to RBI's NEFT Processing Centre
Directly to the beneficiary bank branch

solution.explanation: RBI's FAQs set out the flow: the originating bank sends the message to its pooling centre (NEFT Service Centre), which forwards it to the NEFT Processing Centre operated by RBI for the next batch. The Processing Centre sorts transactions beneficiary bank-wise, passes accounting entries, and sends remittance messages to beneficiary banks through their pooling centres.
solution.why_others_wrong: Messages do not go directly to the beneficiary branch, to NPCI, or through RTGS.
solution.final_answer: Option C: To its pooling centre (NEFT Service Centre), which forwards it to RBI's NEFT Processing Centre

fact_checks.claim: Step-2: The originating bank prepares a message and sends the message to its pooling centre, also called the NEFT Service Centre. Step-3: The pooling centre forwards the message to the NEFT Processing Centre, operated by the RBI

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text:
Consider the following statements about NEFT and IFSC:
I. NEFT can be used for transfers from and to NRE and NRO accounts, subject to FEMA and wire transfer guidelines.
II. The remitter's name must be printed in the beneficiary's account statement or passbook.
III. RBI allocates every branch-level IFSC itself; banks cannot create additional IFSCs.
Which of the above is/are correct?

solution.explanation: NEFT may be used for NRE/NRO accounts subject to FEMA (I correct), and the remitter's name shall be printed in the beneficiary's statement/passbook (II correct). Since core banking, RBI allocates only the primary IFSC (bank code); banks create, modify or delete additional IFSCs for their branches through IFTAS (III wrong).
steps: III: wrong (banks create branch IFSCs via IFTAS)
solution.why_others_wrong: III is false, so options including it are wrong; 'I only' omits II.
solution.final_answer: Option A: I and II only

fact_checks.claim: NEFT can be used to transfer funds from/to NRE and NRO accounts subject to FEMA and Wire Transfer Guidelines; the remitter's name shall be printed in the Account Statement / Pass Book of the beneficiary
RBI now allocates only the primary IFSC representing bank code, and banks can create / modify / delete additional IFSCs for their own branches through IFTAS

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: Why are payments through RTGS final and irrevocable?

options.text: Because they are netted at the end of the day
Because the beneficiary must confirm each payment
Because funds settlement takes place in the books of RBI

solution.explanation: RBI's FAQs state that since the funds settlement takes place in the books of the Reserve Bank of India, RTGS payments are final and irrevocable.
steps: Settlement in RBI's books → final and irrevocable
solution.why_others_wrong: NPCI does not run RTGS; beneficiaries do not confirm; RTGS settles gross, without netting.
solution.final_answer: Option D: Because funds settlement takes place in the books of RBI

fact_checks.claim: Considering that the funds settlement takes place in the books of the RBI, the payments are final and irrevocable

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: What is the 'positive confirmation' feature in RTGS?

options.text: The remitter confirms the beneficiary's name before sending
The beneficiary bank sends an acknowledgement of credit, passed to the remitting bank through RTGS/SFMS so it can inform its customer
The receiving bank confirms the payment before it is settled
RBI confirms every payment by SMS to the beneficiary

solution.explanation: Positive confirmation is a facility under which the beneficiary bank sends an acknowledgement of credit to the beneficiary account; it is communicated to the remitting bank through the RTGS/SFMS messaging arrangement, so the remitting bank can tell its customer the money has been credited.
solution.why_others_wrong: Name verification before sending is the account name look-up facility; RBI does not SMS beneficiaries; confirmation follows the credit, not settlement.
solution.final_answer: Option B: The beneficiary bank sends an acknowledgement of credit, passed to the remitting bank through RTGS/SFMS so it can inform its customer

fact_checks.claim: Positive confirmation is a facility under which the beneficiary bank sends an acknowledgement of credit to the beneficiary account. The acknowledgement is communicated to the remitting bank through the RTGS/SFMS messaging arrangement

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: According to RBI's Payment System Report (May 2026), RTGS accounted for what share of payment transaction value and volume in H2 of CY 2025?

options.text: 68.6% of value but only 0.1% of volume

solution.explanation: RTGS handled 68.6% of the value of payment transactions in H2 2025 but only 0.1% of volume, reflecting its role as a high-value, low-volume system.
solution.why_others_wrong: 85.5% is UPI's volume; 14.9%/3.6% are NEFT's shares; 9.5%/85.5% are UPI's.
solution.final_answer: Option A: 68.6% of value but only 0.1% of volume

fact_checks.claim: RTGS accounted for a mere 0.1 per cent [of volume]... in terms of transaction value, RTGS dominated with 68.6 per cent of the total transaction value

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text:
Consider the following statements from RBI's RTGS FAQs:
I. The beneficiary bank account name look-up facility lets a remitter verify the beneficiary's name as registered in the bank's CBS before transferring funds, and it is free.
II. RTGS members must use prescribed transaction type codes for transactions under the Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Act, 2010.
III. Compensation for a delayed return of an RTGS payment is calculated at the Bank Rate plus 2%.
Which of the above is/are correct?

solution.explanation: The name look-up facility is free and lets a remitter verify the account holder's name before transferring (I correct). Prescribed transaction type codes must be used for FCRA transactions (II correct). Compensation for delay is at the current repo rate plus 2%, not the Bank Rate plus 2% (III wrong).
solution.why_others_wrong: III uses the wrong benchmark, so options including it fail; 'I only' omits II.
solution.final_answer: Option A: I and II only

fact_checks.claim: Beneficiary bank account name look-up facility is a free facility which allows a remitter to verify the beneficiary bank's account holder's name before initiating a fund transfer; RTGS members must use the prescribed transaction type codes for FCRA transactions; compensation at current repo rate plus 2%

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text:
Which of the following single RTGS payments must carry the Legal Entity Identifier (LEI) of both the remitter and the beneficiary?
P. ₹60 crore from a company to another company
Q. ₹75 crore from one individual to another individual
R. ₹55 crore from a Government-owned corporation to a supplier firm
S. ₹40 crore from a company to a partnership firm

solution.explanation: All single NEFT/RTGS payments of ₹50 crore and above undertaken by entities (non-individuals) must include remitter and beneficiary LEI. It is not needed where both parties are individuals (Q), or below ₹50 crore (S). Government departments are exempt, but Government corporations and undertakings must obtain LEI (R needs it).
solution.why_others_wrong: Q involves only individuals; S is below the ₹50 crore threshold; P alone misses R.
solution.final_answer: Option B: P and R only

fact_checks.claim: All single payment transactions of ₹50 crore and above undertaken by entities (non-individuals) should include remitter and beneficiary LEI; not required where both remitter and beneficiary are individuals; Corporations / Undertakings, including those fully owned by the Government, shall need to obtain LEI

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: IMPS, introduced in 2010, made India which country in the world to introduce such a 24x7 fast payment system?

options.text: Fourth, after South Korea, the UK and South Africa

solution.concept: IMPS as a fast payment system
solution.explanation: RBI's payments booklet says IMPS is a 24x7 'fast payments' system introduced in 2010, and India was the fourth country, after South Korea, the UK and South Africa, to introduce such a system.
steps: India: fourth, after South Korea, UK, South Africa
solution.why_others_wrong: India was not the first; the other rankings are not what RBI records.
solution.final_answer: Option B: Fourth, after South Korea, the UK and South Africa

fact_checks.claim: IMPS is a 24*7 'fast payments' system that was introduced in 2010. India was the fourth country after South Korea, UK and South Africa to introduce such a payment system

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: Which of the following is true of participation in IMPS, as described by RBI?

options.text: Besides banks, non-bank entities such as PPI issuers can participate, enabling remittances from wallets to bank accounts
Only scheduled commercial banks can participate
It can be used only through mobile phones
Both remitter and beneficiary must still be registered for mobile banking

solution.explanation: IMPS is multi-channel (mobile, ATM, internet banking, branches, BCs). Besides banks, it allows non-bank entities such as PPI issuers to participate. The early requirement that both parties register for mobile banking was later removed.
steps: Mobile banking registration no longer needed for both parties
solution.why_others_wrong: Non-banks can participate; channels go beyond mobile; the dual-registration requirement was an early feature.
solution.final_answer: Option A: Besides banks, non-bank entities such as PPI issuers can participate, enabling remittances from wallets to bank accounts

fact_checks.claim: IMPS is a multi-channel system that can be accessed using mobile, ATM, internet banking, bank branches, BCs, etc. Besides banks, the system allows non-bank entities such as PPI issuers to participate

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: According to RBI's Payment System Report (May 2026), how did the value of IMPS transactions change between CY 2021 and CY 2025?

options.text: It fell from ₹75 lakh crore to ₹38 lakh crore
It roughly doubled, from ₹38 lakh crore to ₹75 lakh crore
It rose from ₹72 lakh crore to ₹300 lakh crore
It stayed flat at about ₹50 lakh crore

solution.explanation: IMPS volume rose from 434 crore in CY 2021 to 518 crore in CY 2025, while value doubled from ₹38 lakh crore to ₹75 lakh crore (CAGR 4.5% in volume and 18.1% in value). Its larger average size shows it is preferred for medium- to large-value transfers.
solution.why_others_wrong: The second option reverses the trend; 72 → 300 lakh crore is UPI; value did not stay flat.
solution.final_answer: Option B: It roughly doubled, from ₹38 lakh crore to ₹75 lakh crore

fact_checks.claim: IMPS transactions volume rose from 434 crore in CY 2021 to 518 crore in CY 2025... transaction value doubled from ₹38 lakh crore to ₹75 lakh crore

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: In CY 2025, IMPS handled 518 crore transactions worth ₹75 lakh crore, while UPI's average ticket size was ₹1,313. What was IMPS's approximate average ticket size, and about how many times UPI's was it?

solution.explanation: ₹75 lakh crore = 75 × 10⁵ crore rupees. Divide by 518 crore transactions: 75,00,000 ÷ 518 ≈ ₹14,479, about ₹14,500. Ratio to UPI: 14,479 ÷ 1,313 ≈ 11. RBI notes IMPS is preferred for medium- to large-value transfers.
solution.why_others_wrong: ₹1,450 and ₹1,45,000 misplace the decimal; 5 times is an arithmetic slip.

fact_checks.claim: IMPS: 518 crore transactions, ₹75 lakh crore in CY 2025; average transaction size under IMPS is higher than that of UPI; UPI average ticket size ₹1313 in CY 2025

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: Since December 2013, NPCI has operated which system on behalf of RBI?

solution.explanation: RBI's payments booklet records that in December 2013 NPCI was entrusted with operating CTS on behalf of RBI; CTS and the NFS ATM network are NPCI's main revenue sources on the switching side. RTGS, NEFT and e-Kuber are run by RBI.
steps: Dec 2013: NPCI operates CTS for RBI
solution.why_others_wrong: RTGS, NEFT and e-Kuber are RBI systems.

fact_checks.claim: In December 2013, NPCI was entrusted with the task of operating CTS on behalf of RBI

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: The Aadhaar Payments Bridge System (APBS), implemented in 2012, is used mainly for:

options.text: Cash withdrawal at micro-ATMs using biometrics
Crediting government subsidies and benefits to Aadhaar-linked bank accounts

solution.explanation: APBS, a component of NACH implemented in 2012, uses the Aadhaar number to electronically credit government subsidies and benefits to Aadhaar-linked bank accounts. Biometric cash withdrawal at BC points is AePS; toll collection is NETC.
steps: APBS → DBT credits using Aadhaar number
solution.why_others_wrong: Biometric withdrawals are AePS; tolls are NETC/FASTag; cross-border card payments are not APBS.
solution.final_answer: Option D: Crediting government subsidies and benefits to Aadhaar-linked bank accounts

fact_checks.claim: APBS, a component of NACH, which uses Aadhaar number for electronic crediting of government subsidies and benefits in Aadhaar-linked bank account, was implemented in 2012

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: Which of the following payment systems is NOT operated by NPCI?

solution.explanation: NPCI operates retail systems such as IMPS, RuPay, UPI, NACH, AePS, APBS, NETC, *99# and BBPS. RTGS is owned and operated by RBI, with settlement in RBI's books.
steps: NPCI: IMPS, UPI, NACH, AePS, NETC, BBPS, RuPay
solution.why_others_wrong: IMPS, NACH and BBPS are NPCI products.

fact_checks.claim: NPCI has rolled out a variety of innovative retail payment products viz., IMPS, RuPay card scheme, UPI, NACH, AePS, APBS, NETC, *99# (USSD based) and BBPS
RTGS funds settlement takes place in the books of the RBI

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: To widen acceptance abroad, RuPay has tied up with other card networks. With which country's network 'Elo' is it linked?

solution.explanation: RBI's booklet lists RuPay's tie-ups with Union Pay (China), JCB (Japan), NETS (Singapore), BC Card (South Korea), Elo (Brazil) and DinaCard (Serbia), besides Discover and Diners.
solution.why_others_wrong: Serbia's network is DinaCard; Japan's is JCB; South Korea's is BC Card.

fact_checks.claim: RuPay has tied up with Union Pay (China), JCB (Japan), NETS (Singapore), BC Card (South Korea), Elo (Brazil) and DinaCard (Serbia)

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: How are APBS transactions routed to the destination bank?

options.text: Through UIDAI, which settles the funds directly
Through the Aadhaar mapper, a repository of Aadhaar numbers managed by NPCI, using the destination bank's unique Institution Identification Number (IIN)
Through the IFSC of the beneficiary branch entered by the government department
Through the beneficiary's mobile number linked to UPI

solution.explanation: APBS uses the Aadhaar mapper, a repository of Aadhaar numbers managed by NPCI, to route transactions to the destination bank based on its unique IIN. The sponsoring government department needs only the beneficiary's Aadhaar number, not the IFSC or account number.
solution.why_others_wrong: APBS does not need the IFSC; UIDAI does not settle funds; UPI mobile linkage is unrelated.
solution.final_answer: Option B: Through the Aadhaar mapper, a repository of Aadhaar numbers managed by NPCI, using the destination bank's unique Institution Identification Number (IIN)

fact_checks.claim: Aadhaar mapper, a repository of Aadhaar numbers managed by NPCI, is used for routing the APBS transactions to the destination banks based on the unique IIN (Institution Identification Number) of destination bank

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: What minimum paid-up equity capital did RBI's Guidelines for Licensing of Payments Banks (November 2014) prescribe for a payments bank?

solution.explanation: The 2014 licensing guidelines set the minimum paid-up equity capital of a payments bank at ₹100 crore, mainly to buffer operational risk and fund technology, along with a minimum CRAR of 15%.
solution.why_others_wrong: ₹300 crore is the SFB requirement; ₹500 crore and ₹200 crore are not payments bank figures.

fact_checks.claim: Payments bank licensing guidelines: minimum paid-up equity capital Rs. 100 crore

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: Since payments banks work mostly through BCs and ATMs, what outreach requirement did RBI's November 2014 licensing guidelines lay down for them instead of the 25% unbanked rural branch norm?

options.text: At least 25% of physical access points, including BCs, must be in rural centres
At least 50% of branches must be in metropolitan centres
All branches must be in unbanked villages

solution.explanation: The 2014 licensing guidelines did not stipulate that 25% of branches be in unbanked rural centres for payments banks. Instead they required at least 25% of physical access points, including BCs, in rural centres, and a controlling office for clusters of access points.
steps: 25% unbanked rural branch norm: not stipulated
25% of physical access points in rural centres: required
solution.why_others_wrong: There is a requirement; it does not concern metro branches or require all branches in villages.
solution.final_answer: Option A: At least 25% of physical access points, including BCs, must be in rural centres

fact_checks.claim: Payments bank licensing guidelines: 25 per cent unbanked rural branch norm not stipulated; at least 25 per cent of physical access points including BCs to be in rural centres

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: Under RBI's Guidelines for Licensing of Payments Banks (November 2014), could a payments bank distribute mutual fund units and insurance products?

options.text: No, payments banks may only accept deposits
Yes, and it may also underwrite insurance risk
Yes, as non-risk-sharing simple services not requiring its own funds, with RBI's prior approval
Only if it first converts into a small finance bank

solution.explanation: The 2014 guidelines allowed payments banks to undertake other non-risk-sharing simple financial services that do not require commitment of their own funds, such as distribution of mutual fund units, insurance and pension products, with RBI's prior approval and compliance with the sectoral regulator's rules.
steps: Distribution allowed (no own funds, no risk sharing)
solution.why_others_wrong: Distribution is permitted; underwriting risk is not; conversion into an SFB is not required.
solution.final_answer: Option C: Yes, as non-risk-sharing simple services not requiring its own funds, with RBI's prior approval

fact_checks.claim: Payments bank licensing guidelines: non-risk-sharing simple financial services not requiring own funds, such as distribution of mutual fund units, insurance and pension products, with prior RBI approval

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text:
Consider the following statements about payments banks:
I. Under RBI's Payments Banks directions of 2025, they can act as business correspondents of other banks and, with customer consent, transfer deposits above the limit to an account with another bank.
II. RBI's 2014 licensing guidelines allowed them to hold up to 25% of their demand deposit balances in current and time deposits with other scheduled commercial banks.
III. The 2014 licensing guidelines permitted them to handle cross-border personal remittances on the current account.

questions.question_text: An investor puts ₹6,000 a month through a SIP in an equity scheme for three months, when the NAVs are ₹20, ₹30 and ₹24. What is the average cost per unit, and how does it compare with the simple average of the three NAVs?

options.text: ₹24.00, lower than the simple average NAV of about ₹24.67
₹25.00, higher than the simple average NAV
₹22.00, lower than the simple average NAV of ₹24.67
₹24.67, equal to the simple average NAV

solution.explanation: Units bought: 6,000/20 = 300, 6,000/30 = 200, 6,000/24 = 250; total 750 units for ₹18,000. Average cost = 18,000/750 = ₹24.00. The simple average of NAVs is (20+30+24)/3 ≈ ₹24.67. A fixed SIP buys more units when the NAV is low, so the average cost is below the simple average.
solution.shortcut: Average cost of a fixed SIP = harmonic mean of the NAVs.
solution.why_others_wrong: ₹24.67 is the simple average, not the cost; ₹25.00 and ₹22.00 are arithmetic slips.
solution.final_answer: Option A: ₹24.00, lower than the simple average NAV of about ₹24.67
